Reframing Learning Systems: From Difficulty Dials to Cognitive Foraging

Traditional adaptive instructional software treats learning as a linear curriculum with an adjustable difficulty dial—typically tuning item difficulty to target a static ~85% success rate. Cognitive Foraging rejects this model. Human learning is not homogeneous gradient descent; it is an ecological search for useful knowledge patches under resource depletion, memory decay, and structural misconceptions.

⚠ Traditional Adaptive Model

Difficulty Dial
  • ×
    Objective: Maximize immediate item accuracy or target a fixed scalar (e.g., 85% correct).
  • ×
    State Model: Single mastery scalar ($p_k$) that ignores epistemic uncertainty and misconceptions.
  • ×
    Path Rule: Serves standard items continuously until a high threshold is crossed, triggering "wheel-spinning".
  • ×
    Review Logic: External spaced-repetition scheduler fights against the primary mastery controller.

✔ Cognitive Foraging & Wayfinder

Optimal Controller
  • ✓
    Objective: Maximize Expected Transferable Learning per Unit of Attention (ETL/UA).
  • ✓
    State Model: Factored Beta distribution $M_k \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha, \beta)$, variance $\sigma_k^2$, bug vector $\hat{\mu}_k$, and transfer $\hat{\tau}_k$.
  • ✓
    Foraging Rule: Departs a skill patch when marginal rate $\hat{\lambda}_k$ drops below best available alternative.
  • ✓
    Unified Review: Spaced retrieval is organically modeled as patch return during memory regeneration.

The Three Core Questions Wayfinder Answers Continuously

1. Readiness

What is the learner ready to learn next?

Determined via Knowledge Space Theory outer fringes and prerequisite gating.

2. Patch Productivity

Is this patch productive, or should we move?

Calculated by comparing local marginal learning rate $\hat{\lambda}_k$ to switching costs.

3. Transferability

Will this help later, in a new context?

Evaluated via context-transfer coupling matrices and curriculum option value.

7-Dimension Distributional State Model & 4-Scale Coordinator

Wayfinder replaces scalar mastery numbers with a factored Bayesian belief state $\mathcal{B}_t$ across 7 dimensions. To eliminate policy drift, the engine coordinates actions across 4 distinct timescales (Micro, Meso, Macro, Meta).

The 7 Learner Belief State Dimensions ($\mathcal{B}_t$)

1. Mastery Mean & Epistemic Variance
$M_k \sim \text{Beta}(\alpha_k, \beta_k) \implies \sigma_k^2$

High variance triggers diagnostic probes; low variance enables transfer tasks.

2. Misconception Probabilities
$\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k \in [0, 1]^{B_k}$

Tracks active bug patterns. High-confidence errors cause sharp posterior updates.

3. Context Transfer Strength
$\hat{\tau}_{k,t} \in [0, 1] \text{ via } \mathbf{T}$

Measures ability to execute skill in novel contexts; spills over across coupled skills.

4. Memory Stability & Decay Lag
$\hat{S}_{k,t} \in [10, 100], \Delta t_{k,t}$

Elapsed lag discounts concentration parameters; retrieval multiplies stability $\hat{S}_k$.

5. Patch Marginal Rate
$\hat{\lambda}_{k,t} = \Delta p_k / \Delta \text{Attn}$

Exponentially weighted gain rate; triggers MVT patch departure when flattened.

6. Metacognitive Calibration
$\text{BS}_t, \text{Bias} = \frac{1}{W}\sum(c_i - y_i)$

Rolling Brier score and over/underconfidence bias governing contrast case selection.

7. Context & Policy Vector
$\mathbf{g}_t = [\hat{F}_t, \text{Mode}, \text{Budget}]$

Tracks frustration $\hat{F}_t$, help-seeking style, and learner mode vetoes.

The 4-Timescale Coordination Architecture

Micro Scale
Seconds → Minutes

Step hints, immediate feedback, speed-accuracy latency tracking, and representation switches.

Meso Scale
Minutes → Hours

MVT patch departure (stay/leave skill), cognitive role shift (Observer → Practitioner → Reviewer).

Macro Scale
Days → Weeks

Path routing over KST outer fringes, prerequisite challenges, and patch-regeneration review scheduling.

Meta Scale
Weeks → Months

Double-loop calibration graph, help-seeking coaching, and user mode negotiation (Explore/Consolidate).

Productive Surprise Diagnostic Regime

Instead of clamping task accuracy to a single 85% scalar, Wayfinder evaluates accuracy ($y_t$), confidence ($c_t$), and normalized response latency ($z_t$) together to classify learner dynamics into four operational quadrants.

Interactive 2x2 Productive Surprise Matrix (Click any quadrant to test)

High Conf + High Acc + Fast Predictable
Diagnosis: Habituation risk. Minimal prediction error; task is too predictable.
High Conf + Low Acc + Fast/Mod Misconception
Diagnosis: Hypercorrection Window. Active procedural bug executed with high confidence.
Low Conf + High Acc + Slow Fragile
Diagnosis: Unconsolidated Mastery. Correct answer reached via slow trial-and-error.
Low Conf + Low Acc + Slow Chaotic
Diagnosis: Overload / Wheel-Spinning. Task exceeds current schema or prerequisites.

Engineering Implementation Roadmap & Architectural Guardrails

`Wayfinder v1` is designed as a deterministic, auditable, and explainable engine. It does not require opaque deep reinforcement learning to launch, keeping LLMs strictly confined to content and hint generation while retaining policy authority inside the controller.

7-Stage Phased Build Checklist for Wayfinder v1

Stage 1 Beta-BKT + Misconception State Store

Upgrade mastery scalars to Beta distribution parameters $(\alpha_k, \beta_k)$, explicit bug vectors $\hat{\mu}_k$, and temporal concentration decay functions.

Stage 2 3-Step Deterministic MPC Scorer

Implement beam search trajectory planner over horizon $H=3$ using the ETL/UA objective function and discount factor $\gamma=0.92$.

Stage 3 Marginal Value Foraging Rule (MVT)

Track exponentially weighted patch learning rates $\hat{\lambda}_{k,t}$ and switch-cost matrices $c_{\text{switch}}$ to govern patch departure and spaced review.

Stage 4 Productive Surprise Diagnostic UI

Capture fast pre-submission confidence $c_t$ and normalized latency $z_t$ to route through the 4-quadrant diagnostic matrix.

Stage 5 Double-Loop OLM & Agency Mode

Expose inspectable calibration graphs (SMILI☺ framework) and enable user policy modes (Explore/Consolidate/Challenge/Recover).

Stage 6 Multimodal Content Schema Expansion

Attach contrasting cases, guided worked examples, and far-transfer probes to skill nodes; use LLMs strictly for drafting content items.

Architectural Guardrails: What NOT to Do

1. No Independent Heuristics

Never add standalone if/else rules for edge cases. All signals must pass through the unified MPC controller to prevent policy drift.

2. LLMs Cannot Hold Policy Authority

Generative AI models optimize for conversational sycophancy and give away answers. Keep controller decisions strictly deterministic.

3. Do Not Optimize Engagement Alone

Extrinsic gamification (streaks, badges) displaces intrinsic motivation. Treat engagement as a survivability constraint, not the main objective.
